design_critique:
1) The single-variable step (kd 0.9 to 1.2, all else fixed) is a clean test of the raced best (iteration 7, score 122.61). The trend supports a small further gain on the oval: progress rose 0.33, 0.44, 0.50 across kd 0.3, 0.6, 0.9, and the step per kd increment is shrinking (+0.11, then +0.06). Linear extrapolation of that decay suggests roughly +0.02 to +0.03, which is consistent with the expected 0.52 to 0.55. Each +0.03 of oval progress is worth about 4 points on the overall mean, so the 125 to 130 expectation is only reached if oval progress gains at least about 0.02.

2) Oscillation is rising at every step (0.189, 0.246, 0.280). A further rise of about 0.03 to 0.05 is the expected trend, so oscillation near 0.31 to 0.33 is plausible. The design does not say what oscillation level indicates the wheels are saturating or the loop is hunting, so a rise to the 0.33 limit is a judgement, not a measured threshold.

3) Saturation is not measured. The contract gives a derivative of 10 per second per 0.1 signal step at kd 0.9, which is about 9 turn (about 3150 PWM). That already approaches the 4095 limit when added to base PWM near 2870. The step to kd 1.2 therefore adds risk at tape-edge transitions, and the inputs do not report signal step sizes, so the risk is unquantified. Controller_errors does not capture PWM clamping; it counts exceptions only.

4) Noise dominates the per-track means. At kd 0.9 the s-bend ranges from 46 to 194 and the oval from 151 to 339 across trials. A mean shift of 4 to 5 points overall sits well inside that spread, so one race at kd 1.2 cannot show a real gain of this size. The 122.6 keep threshold is a single-point comparison with no noise band.

5) Track balance is unstated. The s-bend rose from 62.3 (kd 0.6) to 117.5 (kd 0.9), and the slalom fell from 41.1 to 36.8 and then to 39.5. The s-bend move is far larger than the oval move and is not explained by the kd change alone. The oval is the only track the design claims to improve, so the overall score may be moved mostly by seed noise on the s-bend.

6) Max_error stays pinned near 0.062 to 0.063 m, above the 0.06 m off-track limit. Every run still ends off track. The 500-point completion term is untouched, base_speed stays at 1.4, and completion_time cannot be defined on off-track runs, so the request does not show whether speed is limiting progress.
rationale_critique:
1) The keep and revert rules overlap and have no precedence. Keep kd 1.2 needs oval progress at least 0.50 and score above 122.6. Revert to 0.9 needs oscillation above 0.33 or progress below 0.50. A run with progress 0.53, score 126 and oscillation 0.34 meets the keep condition and the revert condition at once. The rationale should state which governs.

2) The s-bend and slalom rule is not numeric. The rationale says a fall of more than 10 percent keeps kd 1.2 but names a weakness. The slalom is already at about 39.5 and was 36.8 at kd 0.6, so the 10 percent test needs a stated baseline (iteration 7 or the kd 0.6 run). The rationale does not give one.

3) The claim that a 0.3 kd step is 'small enough to stay clear of the saturation risk' is asserted. The rationale's own earlier reasoning allowed that 0.9 already carries risk. The step should be described as an unmeasured risk, not a safe one.

4) The expected result (score 125 to 130) is a linear extrapolation from three kd points. The rationale does not say this, and it does not state a noise band, so a result of 123 to 127 would be unreadable against the stated thresholds.

5) The justification for completion_time is not valid. Off-track runs have no completion time, so the request will not show whether the robot is slow. The rationale should either drop the claim or say that stall and progress are the only available signals.

6) The rationale defers base_speed and completion again. It names base_speed 1.5 only as a fallback if the score falls, which means the largest term in the objective has no test in this iteration or any stated schedule. With three iterations left after this, the rationale should say when base_speed is tested.
